binders: For every pair of functions pressure, velocity : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ, whose first argument is x and second argument is t.
For every real bulkModulus K, density ρ, spatial coordinate x, and time coordinate t.
On the left side, there exist qt, qx ∈ ℝ², chosen after the functions, parameters, and point are fixed.

On the right side, there exist pt, px, ut, ux ∈ ℝ, in that quantifier order, chosen after the functions, parameters, and point are fixed. These witnesses are local to the right side and are not separately quantified common witnesses across the equivalence.
conclusions: The following statements are equivalent: (A) there exist qt, qx ∈ ℝ² such that τ ↦ q(x,τ) has derivative qt at t, ξ ↦ q(ξ,t) has derivative qx at x, and qt + A qx = (0,0); (B) there exist pt, px, ut, ux ∈ ℝ such that τ ↦ pressure(x,τ) has derivative pt at t, ξ ↦ pressure(ξ,t) has derivative px at x, τ ↦ velocity(x,τ) has derivative ut at t, ξ ↦ velocity(ξ,t) has derivative ux at x, pt + K·ux = 0, and ut + ρ⁻¹·px = 0.
mathematical_definitions: q(ξ,τ) = (pressure(ξ,τ), velocity(ξ,τ)), interpreted as a function Fin 2 → ℝ with indices 0 and 1.
A is the constant real matrix [[0, K], [ρ⁻¹, 0]], where the first index is the row index.
For v = (v0,v1), A v = (K·v1, ρ⁻¹·v0). Vector addition, zero, and scalar multiplication are coordinatewise, and ℝ² carries the product topology.

A derivative assertion means existence of the ordinary derivative of the indicated one-variable slice at its specified real argument. Equivalently, for derivative value d, the difference quotient converges to d as a nonzero real increment tends to zero.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For any two real-valued functions pressure and velocity of two real variables, any real constants K and ρ with ρ nonzero, and any point (x,t), form q = (pressure, velocity) and A = [[0,K],[1/ρ,0]]. The time and space derivatives of q exist at that point and satisfy q_t + A q_x = 0 if and only if all four scalar partial derivatives pressure_t, pressure_x, velocity_t, and velocity_x exist at that point and simultaneously satisfy pressure_t + K·velocity_x = 0 and velocity_t + (1/ρ)·pressure_x = 0.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: Density is required to be nonzero, but need not be positive. Bulk modulus is an arbitrary real number, including zero or negative values.
The functions have domain all of ℝ². The derivatives are ordinary two-sided derivatives of slices, not derivatives restricted to a spatial or temporal subdomain.
The equivalence is pointwise for each universally quantified (x,t). It does not assert that either formulation holds at every point for the chosen functions.
Differentiability is part of each side of the equivalence, not an outer hypothesis. Both sides can be false because a required derivative fails to exist or an equation fails.
At density zero, the implication in the target imposes no conclusion. The definitions themselves still have a meaning because real inversion is totalized at zero.
No joint differentiability, continuity of partial derivatives, higher regularity, initial conditions, boundary conditions, or existence or uniqueness of solutions is asserted.
K and ρ are scalar parameters, not functions of space or time. No derivatives of these coefficients occur.
The variable names do not impose physical units, constitutive assumptions, positivity, or a physical interpretation.
Although the generic vector predicate permits arbitrary finite index types, the target fixes a nonempty two-element index type, so its vector equality has exactly two scalar components.
